subject.title: Multi-profile profile targeting/config truth is ambiguous with ~/.openclaw-* homes on macOS

question: When a user passes root `--profile <name>` for gateway status/restart/install on macOS, should it override inherited `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and profile-derived `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL`, or should those explicit environment values remain authoritative?
rationale: Current code and tests intentionally preserve explicit env/custom label values, while the issue reports that this makes profile-targeted operations untrustworthy; changing precedence affects compatibility, operator-managed labels, and the documented multi-profile story.

options.title: Fail closed on conflicts
options.body: Make `--profile` derive the expected state/config/service target, preserve deliberate custom labels only when unambiguous, and error or warn loudly when inherited env points at a different profile.

options.title: Profile flag always wins
options.body: Treat root `--profile` as an unconditional override for profile-derived state/config/launchd targeting, accepting that some env-first operator workflows may need migration or documentation updates.

options.title: Keep env-first policy
options.body: Leave current precedence intact and document multi-profile operations as requiring clean env or explicit manual env setup, with doctor/status surfacing conflicts instead of changing behavior.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on conflicts
recommendation.body: Make `--profile` derive the expected state/config/service target, preserve deliberate custom labels only when unambiguous, and error or warn loudly when inherited env points at a different profile.
